DEFINITION · qeva:1:measure@1

Measure

A measure assigns a nonnegative size to measurable sets while adding the sizes of disjoint pieces.

editorialmeasure-theory · analysis
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

A measure assigns a nonnegative size to measurable sets while adding the sizes of disjoint pieces.

EXACT

The compact statement

For a measurable space (Ω,𝓕), μ:𝓕→[0,∞] is a measure when μ(∅)=0 and μ(⋃ₙAₙ)=Σₙμ(Aₙ) for every pairwise-disjoint sequence (Aₙ).

Example

Length on intervals extends to Lebesgue measure on a sigma-algebra of subsets of the real line.

Boundary / caveat

A measure needs a declared measurable space; assigning a size to every conceivable subset may be impossible or undesirable.

Assumptions

  • The declared measure theory context is fixed.
